newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks close at calendar year high.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks close at calendar year high.

text.p: Tokyo stocks finished at a high for the calendar year on Monday, as blue chips recovered after early losses brought on by a strong yen, brokers said. They added that the mood was cautious ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee's policy-setting meeting on Tuesday.
The 225-share Nikkei average added 165.02 points or 0.81 percent to 20,489.75. Its June futures rose 180 to 20,550.

"Blue chips revived after initial weakness. Lower priced shares in laggard sectors, real estate issues and futures were bought, giving the indices a strong boost," said Kenji Karikomi at Daiwa Securities.

The Nikkei average slumped to a low of 20,205.62 in the morning, after the yen climbed to near 115 yen in reaction to data showing a surge in Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus for April. Japan's trade surplus more than doubled in April from a year earlier to 831.48 billion yen.

But the yen soon retreated and buying-on-dips and index-linked purchases by institutional investors, including pension funds, appeared, lifting the Nikkei benchmark to an intra-day high of 20,561.66 in the afternoon.
That was the first time the Nikkei rose above the 20,500 line since December 17, when it hit 20,500.90.
"Fundamentals have improved enough for the market to fend off factors such as the strength in the yen and weakness on Wall Street," Keiji Arai, a strategist at Sanyo Securities said.
The Dow industrials shed 1.89 percent on Friday on renewed short-term interest rate jitters.
"Japanese postal savings fund allocations are on the way so sellers are holding off. Also bargain-hunting is active in times of weakness," he added.
Brokers said investors were eager to see the outcome of the FOMC's meeting on Tuesday, which could mean higher U.S. rates.
Turnover was 489 million shares, up slightly from 455 million on Friday. Winners beat losers 685 to 449, while 128 issues were unchanged.

In other indices, TOPIX added 9.54 points or 0.63 percent to end at 1,512.83. The Nikkei 300 rose 1.93 points or 0.66 percent to finish at 292.92. The second section index climbed 10.24 points or 0.59 percent to end at 1,759.26., Second section turnover was 11.08 million shares, little changed from 11.59 million in the previous session.
Keisei Electric Railway Co Ltd rose 27 yen to end at 696, with 7.27 million shares traded.

It was the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse, as investors were drawn to issues in which trade has been somewhat speculative and volume heavy, given the volatile currency market, traders said.

Hopes for a recovery in land prices lifted real estate shares. Tokyu Land Corp rose 17 yen to 446 and Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd 30 yen to 1,500. The gains followed a comment by National Land Agency minister on Friday land prices have almost stabilised after sustained falls.
Earnings results and forecasts continued to steer trade, brokers said.

Chemical firm Denki Kagaku Kogyo KK added 36 yen or 13 percent to end at 316, due to a bright earnings forecast. It was the third largest percentage gainer. By contrast, lamp and optical equipment marker Ushio Inc slipped 170 yen to 1,470 on a cloudy business outlook.

Among blue chips, cars perked up to end with gains. Toyota Motor Corp lost about 40 yen in the morning but finished 80 yen higher at 3,650. Honda Motor Co Ltd shed as much as 50 yen at one point, but clawed up 100 to end at 3,750 yen. Rubber, pulp/paper, mining, real estate and oil were at the top of the list of gaining sectors.
The main declining sectors were miscellaneous manufacturing, warehousing, precision instruments and communications.
-- Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-9052
